body:
Does it happen every time, or only the first `:Explore`?

netrw loves to fiddle with the system clipboard for no reason (in a _loop_).  `:set clipboard=` doesn't help because netrw messes with `@+` explicitly.

This is arguably a netrw bug. We've already worked around the loop issue. Perhaps  `provider/clipboard.vim` could put a `jobwait()` around its xclip attempt so that it times out after 1s.
Also is X11 forwarding functioning when this happens? Is `$DISPLAY` valid? Does `:let @+='foo'` on the remote nvim alter your clipboard?

It's slow also on directory traversal but not that much.

Turns out it's slow only when `DISPLAY` is not empty. After manually fixing `export DISPLAY=` nvim is fast again. I'm not sure how `DISPLAY` could have been corrupted but it could have to do with tmux attaching.

Connecting from an actual X server (cygwin's one) seems to populate `DISPLAY` correctly, but the clipboard afterwards doesn't want to work in either `nvim` or `xclip`:

```console
rr-@cyclone:~$ time echo x | xclip
Error: Can't open display: cyclone:11.0
echo x  0.00s user 0.00s system 0% cpu 0.001 total
clip  0.01s user 0.00s system 0% cpu 3.017 total
```

After these findings I think the issue could be closed as an issue with the environment rather than `nvim`...

issue.title: [RFC] Netrw: Don't try to protect the system clipboard

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
This is a proposed solution for https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/6048.

Netrw tries to protect the system clipboard from accidental changes by
getting and setting the "* and "+ registers. Unfortunately it does this
frequently and Neovim's clipboard provider which uses system() calls to
utilities such as pbcopy and pbpaste just isn't fast enough. After a
quick look through the code I'm reasonably confident that netrw never
touches these registers anyway so we can just skip the saving and
restoring of theese registers.

This fix seems like the simplest way to speed up netrw without big changes that could make it harder to merge future netrw patches from Vim.

---

For reference - rough benchmark comparing how long it takes vim8 to modify OS X clipboard 100 times vs neovim doing the same:

    $ time vim -u NONE +'for i in range(100) | let @* = i | endfor' +qa
    vim -u NONE +'for i in range(100) | let @* = i | endfor' +qa  0.12s user 0.02s system 88% cpu 0.151 total

    $ time nvim -u NONE +'for i in range(100) | let @* = i | endfor' +qa
    nvim -u NONE +'for i in range(100) | let @* = i | endfor' +qa  8.50s user 1.57s system 94% cpu 10.632 total

issue.title: clipboard: avoid pathology during :redir

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
This was quite an adventure.

redir_write():
- ~~This is a "batch" operation which was not yet covered by
  start_batch_changes()~~ This was irrelevant; the problem actually is that `:redir @+>` is an explicit register (as opposed to "implicit" clipboard target with `clipboard=unnamed[plus]`). We can't go around second-guessing explicit register writes, so there is little we can do to avoid invoking the clipboard provider once-per-line during `:redir @+>`.

adjust_clipboard_name():
- msg() and friends during :redir will, of course, cause redir_write()
  to try to capture that message, which causes recursion.
- EMSG() here is trouble: if it interrupts :redir it is a mess.
  Rather than deal with the mess, show a non-error message.

Closes #7182
Closes #7184
ref #6048

issue.title: netrw is slow over ssh
issue.body:
When using vim over SSH with X11 forwarding (might require +clipboard), netrw is really sluggish, taking up to multiple seconds when opening a directory listing.

**To Reproduce**
1. SSH to a remote machine with X11 forwarding 
2. open vim compiled
3. use `:e .` to open the directory listing in netrw
4. optionally change into another directory

steps 3 and 4 should be quite sluggish

**Expected behavior**
I expect netrw to be as quick as without X11 forwarding. If I unset DISPLAY before starting vim, netrw is fast.

**Workaround**
If I execute `let @* = @*` and `let @+ = @+` before opening netrw, netrw is fast. But I have to do this manually. Adding the commands to my vimrc does _not_ fix the problem.

Edit: it also works if I use the `VimEnter` autocommand group to execute the `let` commands, though vim hangs for a short time at startup then.
